intended_object: The diagonal representation k[Gⁿ]: the free k-module on Gⁿ, where G acts by left multiplication on every coordinate, g·(g₁,…,gₙ) = (gg₁,…,ggₙ). It is the representation underlying the standard (bar/homogeneous) resolution in group cohomology. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition is `ofMulAction k G (Fin n → G)`, which is the permutation representation on k[Fin n → G] coming from a G-action on `Fin n → G`. That action is Mathlib's Pi instance, `(g • f) i = g * f i`, so G multiplies every coordinate on the left at once. This is exactly the diagonal action, and the linearised representation is the standard k[Gⁿ]. Using `Fin n` is the usual way to write Gⁿ in the literature. The setting is already broad: any ring k and any monoid G, which is at least as general as the textbook setting of a commutative ring and a group. Edge case: for n = 0, G⁰ is a single point, so the definition gives the trivial representation on k, which is the standard convention. I found no other Mathlib definition of this object.
